name: http_request

url.description:
An https URL on a host the network policy lists. Its whole
host may be written `${secrets.NAME.host}`.

headers.description:
Request headers. `Authorization` may carry `${secrets.NAME.FIELD}`
placeholders, put in place when the request is sent; no other header
may carry one.

body.description: The body, sent as written; it may carry no placeholder.

name: web_fetch

url.description: An HTTPS URL to read under the run's network policy.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters to return. The default output budget also applies.

name: notify

oneOf.description: Delivered without a sound or an alert.
Delivered as the recipient's notifications usually are.
Delivered past the recipient's quiet hours.

anyOf.description: How urgently a notification asks for attention.

name: web_search
description: Search the public web for a query. Returns links, dates and excerpts. Requires public web access under the run's network policy.

query.description: What to search the public web for.

parameters.description: The search text supplied by the model.

name: memory_store
description: Remember a fact for later runs under a stable key.

key.description:
A stable key, such as `incident:42:findings`; storing under it again
replaces what it held.

category.description:
`core` is read first by every later run: name it only for standing
guidance the person's newest message asks you to keep. `daily` expires
after a retention sweep; `note` (the default) and any other label are
kept by recency.

oneOf.description:
Every agent granted to read shared memory, which names this agent as
the writer.

anyOf.description: Who reads a stored memory, as the model names it.

visibility.description:
`private` (the default) keeps it to this agent; `shared` lets other
agents granted shared memory recall it, naming the writer.

name: memory_recall

query.description:
Text to look for in each memory's key and content, ignoring case;
empty matches every memory.

limit.description: The most memories to answer with: 5 when absent.

name: memory_list
memory_forget
description: Forget a remembered fact for the rest of this run. The stored copy stays, including one this run already saved; store the key again to replace it.

name: update_plan

explanation.description: Why the plan changed, when it did.

plan.description: Every step, in order; at most one in progress.

name: ask_user
description: Ask the person a question you cannot answer from what you can read or run, and wait for their answer, which is this call's result. The run pauses until they answer. Ask one question at a time.

question.description:
The question, as the person reads it: one question, with what they
need to answer it.

options.description:
Answers to offer, when the question has a few; the person may still
answer in their own words.

name: message

text.description:
What to tell the people in the conversation now, such as what this
run is doing or waiting for.

name: fleet_steer
description: Ask another fleet in this workspace to do something, by its fleet_id. Returns at once: that fleet runs on its own and can answer with fleet_steer. Read what it did with fleet_activity.

fleet_id.description:
The fleet to ask: its `fleet_id` from `fleet_activity`, or from the
first line of a message another fleet sent this one.

text.description: What to ask it, in plain words. At most 1,048,576 characters.

name: fleet_activity
description: List this workspace's fleets with their status, or, given a fleet_id, that fleet's recent events with an excerpt of what it was asked and what it answered. Wakes no fleet.

fleet_id.description:
A fleet's id, to read its recent events. Omit it to list the
workspace's fleets with their status.

limit.description: How many to read: up to 100 fleets, or up to 25 events.

starting_after.description: The `next_cursor` of the page before, to read the next one.

name: schedule
description: Schedule one more run at a given moment, with a message saying what to do then. It is removed after it runs. Call it only when the person's newest message asks for a later run.

at.description:
When to run again, as an RFC 3339 instant such as
`2026-10-06T09:00:00+05:30`, within the next year. Read to the minute.

message.description: What the run is asked to do then.

name: cron_add
description: Schedule a run on a recurring cron expression, with a message saying what to do each time it fires. Call it only when the person's newest message asks for a recurring run.

cron.description:
Five numeric fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week,
such as `0 9 * * 1` for Mondays at 09:00.

timezone.description: An IANA zone such as `Asia/Kolkata`; UTC when absent.

message.description: What the run is asked to do each time it fires.

name: cron_list
description: List the schedules, each with its expression, zone, message and who made it.

name: cron_remove

schedule_id.description: The schedule's id, as `cron_list` names it.

parameters.description: The arguments naming one schedule: `cron_remove`'s and `cron_run`'s.

name: cron_update

schedule_id.description: The schedule's id, as `cron_list` names it.

paused.description: `true` stops it firing, `false` starts it again.

name: cron_run
description: Run a schedule now, as if it had fired; the run is queued behind this one.

schedule_id.description: The schedule's id, as `cron_list` names it.

parameters.description: The arguments naming one schedule: `cron_remove`'s and `cron_run`'s.

name: cron_runs
description: List the runs a schedule fired, newest first.

schedule_id.description: The schedule's id, as `cron_list` names it.

limit.description: How many runs to read; one page of the backend's size when absent.

starting_after.description: The `next_cursor` of the page before, to read further back.

name: trigger_add
description: Call this tool only when the person's newest message asks for this fleet to wake on something outside it. Do not call it for a question, a greeting or an approval; answer those in plain text. Adds a webhook, a GitHub App event or a Slack mention the workspace has connected; a webhook's URL is in the answer. A webhook's signing secret stays in the workspace vault, named by secret_name: agentsfleetd checks deliveries with it, so this fleet needs no access to it.

oneOf.description: A signed delivery to the fleet's own webhook URL.
An event the workspace's GitHub App delivers.
A mention of the bot in one Slack channel.

source.description:
For `webhook`: the source, the last segment of its URL, such as
`sentry`.

events.description: The event names that wake the fleet; every event when absent.

repositories.description:
For `app_event`: the repositories whose events wake the fleet, as
`owner/name`.

scheme.description: The signing recipe, such as `body-hex-sha256` or `svix-v1`.

header.description:
The header carrying the signature, for a recipe that signs the body
alone.

verifier.description:
For a `webhook` from a source the workspace does not know: how it
signs.

secret_name.description: For `webhook`: the workspace vault key holding its signing secret.

name: trigger_list
description: List the triggers that wake this fleet, each with its id, kind, source and URL.

name: trigger_remove
description: Remove one trigger of this fleet, by its id, only when the person's newest message asks; deliveries to it are refused from then on.

trigger_id.description: The trigger's id, as `trigger_list` names it.

name: request_access
description: Call this tool only when the person's newest message asks for work that needs access to a secret, integration or web host you do not hold. Do not call it for a question, a greeting or an approval; answer those in plain text. Ask for one name in the workspace, such as a vault secret or `github` with its scope, or one bare DNS hostname as `host`. A person approves it once on a card: this run ends waiting, and resumes with their answer.

name.description:
The secret's key in the workspace vault, such as `sentry`, or a
connected integration, such as `github`.

host.description: A bare DNS hostname the fleet needs to reach while reading a page.

scope.description:
For `github` only: `{"repositories": ["owner/name"], "access": "read"}`,
or `"access": "write"` with `"base"`, the branch every pull request
opens against.

name: task_start
description: Call this tool only when the person's newest message asks for work that must keep going past this run, such as fixing something until a check passes. Do not call it for a question, a greeting or an approval; answer those in plain text. Starts a task from the span of their message that asks for it, judged done against the statements you write; its first run follows this one.

title.description: A short name a person reads in the fleet's task list.

source_turn_id.description: The person's message the task comes from. Defaults to the newest message.

source_start.description: Where the task's objective starts in that message, in UTF-8 bytes.

source_end.description: Where it ends, exclusive, in UTF-8 bytes.

oneOf.description: Work through the HTTP tools, with no repository checked out.
Work on one open pull request the person named.

items.description: One yes-or-no statement the task is judged done against.

id.description:
A stable key, such as `checks-green`: letters, digits, `_`, `.` and
`-`, unique within the task.

question.description: The question, such as "Do PR 88's required checks pass on its head?".

statements.description: What must hold for the task to be done: at least one.

name: task_input
description: Call this tool only when the person's newest message steers one of the fleet's unfinished tasks the prompt lists. Do not call it for a question, a greeting or an approval; answer those in plain text. Hands the span of their message that steers it to that task, which reads it at its next step.

durable_task_id.description: The unfinished task, as the prompt lists it.

source_turn_id.description: The person's message that steers it. Defaults to the newest message.

source_start.description: Where the steering text starts in that message, in UTF-8 bytes.

source_end.description: Where it ends, exclusive, in UTF-8 bytes.

name: shell
description: Run one shell command in the working directory and read back its output and exit code. The command is killed once timeout_ms passes. To keep a process running across calls, use exec_command.

command.description: The command, as `sh -c` runs it in the working directory.

timeout_ms.description: How long it may run, in milliseconds: 10000 when absent.

name: exec_command
description: Start a shell command in the working directory and keep it running across calls. Answers with the output that arrived within yield_time_ms and, while the process runs, its session ID; use write_stdin to send it input or read more. The session ends when the process exits or the run ends.

workdir.description:
The directory to run it in, relative to the working directory; the
working directory itself when absent.

tty.description:
Whether to run it on a pseudo-terminal, for a program that needs one;
pipes when absent.

yield_time_ms.description: How long to wait for output before answering, in milliseconds: 10000 when absent, between 250 and 30000.

max_output_tokens.description:
The most output tokens to read back: 10000 when absent, at most
262144.

name: write_stdin
description: Write to a session exec_command started and read back what it printed within yield_time_ms. Send empty chars to only read. Answers the exit code once the process has ended.

session_id.description: The session id an earlier `exec_command` answered with.

chars.description: What to write to the process's input; empty to only read what arrived.

yield_time_ms.description: How long to wait for output before answering, in milliseconds: 10000 when absent, between 250 and 30000; an empty write waits at least 5000.

max_output_tokens.description:
The most output tokens to read back: 10000 when absent, at most
262144.

name: git
description: Run git on the repository checked out in the working directory and read back its output and exit code. Local commands only: push, fetch, pull, remote and clone are refused, because this environment does not reach the repository's remote.

args.description:
The arguments after `git`, one per element, such as
`["log", "--oneline", "-5"]`.

timeout_ms.description: How long it may run, in milliseconds: 10000 when absent.

name: file_read
description: Read a file in the working directory and read back its text: at most `limit` lines from line `offset` (1 when absent), cut to the same output budget as a command's. A read that stops before the file ends says on its last line which offset to read on from.

path.description: The file, relative to the working directory.

offset.description: The line to start at, counting from 1: the first when absent.

limit.description: The most lines to read: 2000 when absent.

name: file_write

path.description:
The file, relative to the working directory; missing directories are
made.

name: file_edit

path.description: The file, relative to the working directory.

old_text.description:
The text to replace, exactly as the file holds it; the file must hold
it once.

edits.description:
The replacements, at least one. Each is matched against the file as
it was before this call, and no two may overlap.

name: apply_patch
description:
Edit files using add, update or delete hunks in one patch. Paths are relative to the working directory. Every hunk is checked before changes are written. The answer lists the files and line counts. Prefer file_edit for a single exact replacement or file_write to create or replace a whole file.
Example arguments
{"patch":"*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: notes.md
+Ready for review.
*** End Patch"}

patch.description:
The patch: `*** Begin Patch`, then hunks, then `*** End Patch`. A hunk
is `*** Add File: <path>` with `+` lines, `*** Delete File: <path>`,
or `*** Update File: <path>` with `@@ <context>` markers and ` `, `-`
and `+` lines; `*** Move to: <path>` after an update renames the file.
Paths are relative to the working directory.

name: image
description: Look at an image file in the working directory: PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP. The image is shown to you with this call's result on your next step. One longer than 2048 pixels on a side is scaled down to fit.

path.description:
The image file, relative to the working directory: PNG, JPEG, GIF or
WebP.

name: browser
description: Act on the open page in the environment's browser: click, type, scroll, read. An environment with no browser refuses the call with a code, and the run continues.

name: browser_open
description: Open a page in the environment's browser. An environment with no browser refuses the call with a code, and the run continues.

name: screenshot
description: Take a screenshot of the open page in the environment's browser. An environment with no browser refuses the call with a code, and the run continues.

name: spawn_agent

message.description: The child's first task, as the message it reads.

tools.description:
The tools the child holds, each one you hold; every one you hold when
absent.

fork_turns.description:
How much of your history the child starts from, before its task:
`all` (the default) for every turn, `none` for its task alone, or a
number for your last that many turns.

name: send_input
description: Queue a message for a child agent: a running child reads it on its next step, an idle one with its next task. Answers whether it was accepted; a closed child accepts none. To give an idle child work, use followup_task.

parameters.description: A child named by the id `spawn_agent` answered, and a message for it.

name: followup_task
description: Give a child agent another task. An idle child runs again with its whole history; a running one reads the task on its next step. Answers whether it was accepted; a closed child accepts none.

parameters.description: A child named by the id `spawn_agent` answered, and a message for it.

name: wait_agent
description: Wait for a child agent's turn to end and read its answer. Answers its status, with its answer once done or its detail once failed, and running when the timeout passed first.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for the child's turn to end, in milliseconds: 30000 when absent, at most 3600000; 0 only looks.

name: list_agents
description: List every child agent of this run: its agent_id, status, depth and how many calls it made.

name: close_agent
description: Close a child agent, and every child it started, once it is no longer needed. A closed child keeps no history and frees its place, so another may start. Answers its status before it closed.

parameters.description: A child named by the id `spawn_agent` answered.

name: interrupt_agent
description: Interrupt a child agent's current turn, if it runs one, and answer its status before. The child stays open for messages and follow-up tasks.

parameters.description: A child named by the id `spawn_agent` answered.
